description: D³ VITAL-X is an independent research prototype for space & astronaut health-indicator data exploration, unifying time-series, image & biomedical datasets with edge AI, entropy analysis & anomaly scoring.
summary:
D³ VITAL-X is an AI-assisted Space Intelligence Platform developed to explore data-driven approaches to astronaut health monitoring and scientific signal analysis.

The platform combines two research workflows: biomedical signal analysis using PhysioNet ECG benchmarks and recorded physiological noise, and astrophysical data inspection using NASA/MAST James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) NIRSpec FITS science products.

Its analytical capabilities include data quality assessment, entropy and variance analysis, coupling dynamics, transition analysis, noise-resilience testing, and exploratory anomaly screening.

A project-generated 80,000-row biomedical stress-test dataset enables controlled evaluation of signal-processing workflows under three recorded noise conditions.

By integrating heterogeneous scientific datasets into a modular analytical framework, D³ VITAL-X aims to explore accessible computational tools for future astronaut health-monitoring research.

This is an independent research prototype, not a medical diagnostic or flight-certified system.
details:
D³ VITAL-X is an independent research prototype built around a modular architecture for scientific data ingestion, quality assessment, feature extraction, signal analysis, and interactive visualization.

The platform integrates two distinct analytical workflows.

BIOMEDICAL WORKFLOW: The biomedical pipeline uses the PhysioNet MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (Record 100) and MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database. Three recorded noise conditions—Baseline Wander (BW), Electrode Motion (EM), and Muscle/EMG Noise (MA)—were used to generate a controlled biomedical stress-test dataset.

The resulting dataset contains 80,000 rows and 10 columns, with two ECG leads and six independently noise-affected channels. The target and measured aggregate signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) were 10 dB.

SPACE SCIENCE WORKFLOW: The astrophysical pipeline uses NASA/MAST JWST NIRSpec calibrated (CAL) and two-dimensional spectral (S2D) FITS science products. Dedicated components support FITS inspection, metadata extraction, data-quality checks, science-product routing, and exploratory analysis.

ANALYTICAL CAPABILITIES: • Entropy and variance analysis. • Coupling and transition analysis. • Signal quality assessment. • Controlled noise-resilience evaluation. • Exploratory anomaly screening. • Data visualization and structured reporting. • Data provenance and reproducibility documentation.

TECHNOLOGY: Python, Streamlit, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Astropy, Google Colab, and GitHub.

CREATIVE APPROACH AND INTENDED IMPACT: The project's central innovation is a unified, modular signal-analysis architecture that explores heterogeneous scientific datasets through reusable analytical components. It emphasizes lightweight computation, transparent data processing, and research reproducibility.

The biomedical stress-test dataset is derived from public human-ECG benchmarks and is not astronaut-specific medical data. JWST observations are astrophysical science products, not astronaut physiological measurements.

D³ VITAL-X aims to explore computational approaches that may support future astronaut health-monitoring research. Its outputs are exploratory analytical indicators, not medical diagnoses, confirmed anomalies, or flight-certified assessments.
